open_obligations: Check Irving et al.'s original rule that a judge should vote against a debater caught in a lie
Note that assigning answers changes incentives relative to Irving et al.'s self-chosen answers, so equilibrium arguments may not transfer directly
Read p13 L44-52 for the authors' full reasoning on relaxing the lie rule

Check who the debaters are and how a debate ends in Michael et al., since the cited passage does not say, whereas Irving et al.'s simplest game has two agents that take turns making statements s0 to s(n-1) before the judge decides
out.other_title: Definition of the two-agent debate game (answers, alternating statements, judge)
out.rationale: The passage explicitly says the approach builds on Irving et al. and lists the changes, which is the definition of EXTENDS. The third change relaxes Irving et al.'s restriction that judges should automatically vote against a debater caught in a lie.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: Debate protocol design; the changes are made for information-asymmetric reading comprehension; in Michael et al. the judge interacts with the debaters between each turn to state beliefs, ask questions and make requests, whereas Irving et al.'s judge sees the debate (q, a, s) and then decides which agent wins

text: The authors say their approach builds on Irving et al.'s (2018) AI safety via debate proposal, with notable differences: debaters are assigned answers rather than choosing them, the judge interacts with debaters between turns, and judges are not required to automatically vote against a debater caught in a lie.
title: Michael et al. build on Irving et al.'s debate: assigned answers, judge interaction, softer lie rule
